Voice pipelines, wake words, and more
Once connected to Home Assistant, Ava gains full pipeline switching, real-time wake word model tuning, remote speaker diagnostics, and unlocks future advanced voice control capabilities

The voice pipeline is Home Assistant\'s understanding path, a command goes through two sides from wake to action: the device handles wake and recording, this page\'s pipeline handles speech-to-text, understanding, and spoken reply, four fields set language, speech-to-text, conversation agent, and text-to-speech separately, pipeline alerts can be corrected here by changing the engine or language

Ava Pro characteristic custom deep intelligent front-and-backup technology, three-tier interface characteristic definition of large language models, can call the device offline small model directly, keep device privacy and safety

Feature intro: the default first choice is Home Assistant native pipeline conversation understanding. More setup is on the Home Assistant web page, Settings - Voice assistants, edit the assistant in use and it takes effect at once. Fast custom changes, the second option is connecting a global remote LLM, the logic is prompt characteristic definition of on-device functions, it can really control music playback and so on without complex operations

Ava acts as a voice satellite, sending microphone audio to the Home Assistant pipeline for speech recognition, intent understanding and execution. Conversation ability depends on the conversation agent configured on the HA web UI — edit it under HA Settings → Voice assistants and changes take effect immediately.
Configure the Home Assistant server URL and token on the home page first

Speech recognition is still handled by Home Assistant, but conversation understanding is handled by your configured remote LLM (Claude / OpenAI / Ollama). The LLM controls devices through built-in Ava Pro exclusive tool calls (such as music playback), and commands are grounded to HA entities locally. A Home Assistant token must be configured on the home page to control other home devices.

On non-root Android, TTS cannot use a separate volume path Speech and music share system media volume Ava Pro temporarily rewrites that volume during a reply so speech can duck the music source, then restores it when speech ends
System volume above is adjustable, and the device volume keys update it live TTS volume below is the reply target Compare the two bars to see whether speech will be louder or quieter than music

When a reply starts, system volume jumps to the current TTS level Dragging TTS volume or changing the Home Assistant entity changes loudness immediately, and the system volume bar moves with it Changing system volume or pressing volume keys during the reply only remembers where to restore after speech; it does not change the current speech level When TTS ends, system volume returns to the value remembered at the start (or the value queued during speech) That memory is a per-reply snapshot, not a saved media-volume preference

With Show in Home Assistant on, Ava publishes config entity number.<device>_tts_volume (10–100, input box) Automations can change TTS by time, scene, or other conditions; updates take effect immediately

Example: quieter TTS at night

alias: Night TTS
trigger:
 - platform: time
 at: "22:00:00"
action:
 - service: number.set_value
 target:
 entity_id: number.ava_tts_volume
 data:
 value: 25

Example: adapt to current media volume (media 80 → TTS about 40)

alias: TTS half of media
trigger:
 - platform: state
 entity_id: media_player.ava
 attribute: volume_level
action:
 - service: number.set_value
 target:
 entity_id: number.ava_tts_volume
 data:
 value: "{{ [[(state_attr('media_player.ava', 'volume_level') | float(0.5) * 50) | int, 10] | max, 100] | min }}"
The temporary rewrite applies only to TTS / wake playback Music and other media return to the remembered system volume after speech, and are not permanently left at the TTS level

Reports occupied once probability passes the threshold, streamed live to Home Assistant
%1$s is off Turn it on at %2$s, then come back and check this tile
Ava\'s built-in Bayesian occupancy sensor: it merges the on-device signals you already use into one answer — is someone in the room — steadier than any single motion sensor
Tiles stay gray until that feature is on; tap one to see where to enable it Once enabled, check the tile and it joins the inference More sources, better judgment

Threshold is how sure it must be before reporting occupied — higher is stricter, lower is more sensitive Decay is the minimum quiet time before the room counts as empty — it is a floor: the longer someone has been around, the longer the hold stretches, so sitting still never marks you gone

Four layers Bayes: every signal carries its own weight of evidence — a detected face is near-certain proof, a faint desk vibration only a weak hint — and evidence stacks probabilistically, so one weak signal can\'t fool it Hive inertia: sustained activity builds confidence, so the longer you\'ve been in the room the more patiently it waits before declaring it empty, while a brief walk-through fades fast Causal hysteresis: turning occupied requires crossing the threshold, turning empty requires falling below a lower release line, so the state never flickers House prior: multiple Avas share their state over the local network, so when another room just saw someone, this room knows a person is home and believes its first signals sooner — and when the whole house is quiet, it doubts weak signals instead

Once enabled, a Bayesian Occupancy sensor appears under the Ava device\'s diagnostics in Home Assistant Use it as a condition: lights on and photo wall back when someone\'s there; lights off, music paused and screen dimmed once the room stays empty Sitting still won\'t get you marked as gone

The Mod Store installs and manages extension modules It supports both special hardware and general Android device enhancements, and can continuously expand what Ava can do The top tabs are Catalog, Manage, and Updates: Catalog browses and downloads online, Manage shows installed mods and local import, Updates lists mods with a newer store version

You can build custom modules with GPIO, system interfaces, service calls, and open-source components, then use AI-assisted design and debugging to extend device attributes, automation flows, and Ava interaction logic

When you are offline, built a mod yourself, or cannot download from the store, pack the mod as a zip and import it on the Manage tab Official release packages live at https://github.com/knoop7/ava-mods

1 Understand the folder layout
Ava installs from the mods tree, not sources (sources is for developers) Two kinds of packages:
mods/devices/<device-mod>/ for device-specific mods
mods/features/<feature-mod>/ for general features

Open any published folder The smallest package looks like Sticky Note:
sticky-note/
 manifest.json (tells Ava the mod id, version, and which files to load)
 libs/
 sticky-note-manager.jar (the code that runs)

Some mods also ship native libraries, for example AirPlay:
airplay-receiver/
 manifest.json
 libs/
 airplay-receiver-manager.jar
 jni/
 arm64-v8a/ (.so files)
 armeabi-v7a/ (.so files)
Those .so files must be inside the zip too Do not ship the jar alone

2 How manifest.json and libs fit together
Open manifest.json in a text editor Find the "libs" list, for example "libs/sticky-note-manager.jar" Every relative path in that list must exist inside the zip, unchanged The "id" field is the unique mod name Importing the same id again replaces the on-disk files, your Ava config for that mod is usually kept

3 Make the zip (pick one way)
Recommended on a computer:
1) Open the repo folder, e.g mods/features/sticky-note/
2) Confirm manifest.json and the libs folder are both there
3) Zip from inside that folder:
 macOS / Linux: zip -r sticky-note.zip manifest.json libs
 Windows: select manifest.json and libs, then Compress to ZIP
4) You should get sticky-note.zip After unzipping, you should see manifest.json immediately, or one folder that contains it Both layouts work

You may also zip the whole sticky-note folder Do not nest many extra parent folders, and do not zip only the jar without manifest.json

4 Copy to the phone and import
1) Copy the zip to the phone (USB, cloud drive, or Files)
2) In Ava open Settings, Advanced, Mod Store
3) Open the Manage tab
4) Tap Import mod at the top of the list
5) Pick the zip, wait for success, grant permissions if asked (voice service may restart)

5 Tips

Ava Pro needs permission to call Home Assistant actions (media volume, weather forecast, quick entities, and more) New ESPHome devices leave this off by default:
In Home Assistant open **Settings - Devices & services - ESPHome**, find this Ava Pro device, then tap **Configure**
Enable **Allow the device to perform Home Assistant actions**, then submit HA reconnects the device and the features start working again
Only turn this on if you **trust this device** Without it, HA rejects Ava Pro service calls and related features stay silent

The current voice assistant uses the **default Assist intent library** (fixed sentence matching only) Unrecognized commands return a \"could not understand\" reply To enable natural-language conversation, switch the **Conversation agent** (optional):
Open HA **Settings - Voice assistants**, edit the assistant, and set **Conversation agent** to an already-configured AI provider (OpenAI, Google AI, Claude, Ollama, etc.)
Optional: the community integration **Claw Assistant** can also enhance conversation capabilities Tap **Next** for details and installation steps

**Claw Assistant** (`ha-china/ha_claw`) is an optional open-source HA custom integration that adds LLM multi-turn tool calling to Assist Not required for normal Ava Pro operation:
Install via **HACS**: add repository `ha-china/ha_claw`, install **Claw Assistant**, restart Home Assistant Requires HA 2025.12+ and at least one configured AI conversation agent
Manual install: place the `claw_assistant` directory under `config/custom_components/`, restart HA, then add the integration in **Settings - Devices & services**
After installation, set the assistant **Conversation agent** to Claw Assistant in **Settings - Voice assistants**, then test voice via Ava Pro

Open HA **Settings - Voice assistants**, open the **assistant** used by this device (see **Assist devices** for the device-to-assistant mapping)
Confirm **Speech-to-text**, **Text-to-speech**, and **Conversation agent** select available engines, and that each **Language** matches the assistant **Language**, then tap **Update**
Return to Ava Pro and test voice again
